text:
Morgan: Heads-up — onboarding hit: sampleapp's CLI accepts REDWOOD_API_KEY but our Python SDK examples use REDWOOD_KEY. New users get a 401 during the quickstart :grimacing:
Elaine: Ugh, that mismatch will bite a lot of folks. Which SDKs are out of sync?
Raj: Python and node examples both use `REDWOOD_KEY` right now. CLI and some infra scripts still check `REDWOOD_API_KEY` and `RW_API_KEY`.
Isabel: I saw this in support too — users copy paste from different docs and end up with the wrong env var. Onboarding flow should be deterministic.
DevexBot: Reminder: config spec v0.9 recommends a canonical env var but allows backwards-compatible fallbacks. See https://internal.redwood/config/spec
Morgan: Proposal: unify order-of-precedence across SDKs/CLI (env var lookup order): 1) RW_API_KEY 2) REDWOOD_API_KEY 3) REDWOOD_KEY 4) credentials file (~/.redwood/credentials) 5) metadata provider (GCP/AWS). That keeps short name first while retaining compatibility. Thoughts?
Elaine: That order seems fine. Put RW_API_KEY first because it's already used in many guides and shorter to type. Make sure we log a clear error listing which vars we looked for.
Raj: Also need to standardize org/project scoping behavior. Right now some tools expect `REDWOOD_ORG` + `REDWOOD_PROJECT`, others read these from the key payload. We should prefer explicit env vars if present, otherwise fall back to key-embedded scoping.
Isabel: Agreed. For rotation, recommend supporting optional `REDWOOD_KEY_ID` header so ops can rotate keys without changing env var names. SDKs should expose an automatic rotate callback/refresh provider for long-running processes.
Morgan: Quick technical note for engineers: current python logic is basically:
```python
# cli
key = os.getenv("REDWOOD_API_KEY") or os.getenv("RW_API_KEY")
# python sdk examples (old)
client = Client(api_key=os.environ["REDWOOD_KEY"])  # raises KeyError
```
That explains the 401s — SDK raises instead of falling back.
Elaine: So we should change SDKs to attempt fallbacks and not throw KeyError mid-quickstart. Also add a helpful message: "No API key found — tried RW_API_KEY, REDWOOD_API_KEY, REDWOOD_KEY. See https://docs.redwood/keys for how to create one."
Raj: For parity: add the same lookup helper in all official SDKs (py/js/go/ruby). One helper -> tests -> docs updated.
Isabel: I'll add an integration test that spins the sampleapp with env var permutations so we don't regress.
Morgan: Can we also add telemetry when a fallback is used? Non-identifying: e.g., `env_key_confidence: fallback` so we can see how often mismatches happen.
Elaine: Fine as long as it's opt-out by env var (PII policy).
DevexBot: New task created: DE-4237 "Unify env var lookup + key rotation support" assigned to @Isabel, @Raj.
Isabel: I'll open a small PR for the python and node SDKs to implement the lookup helper and add the error message. Will also update the sampleapp quickstart.
Morgan: Thanks — can you also add a short CLI migration note (1-liner) so users know both vars are supported for 3 months?
Isabel: Yep. I'll include the deprecation window and a link to the docs and a sample `export` block.
Raj: I'll coordinate with security for the `REDWOOD_KEY_ID` header format and rotation docs.
Elaine: Awesome. Quick checklist for PRs: unit tests for lookup order, integration test for sampleapp, error message text, docs snippet, telemetry opt-out flag.
Morgan: Perfect. If anyone hits this in support before the fix lands, ping me and I'll point them to a temp workaround: set `RW_API_KEY` to your key. :thumbsup:
